body:
## Problem

One of the problems with netrw is that it tried to do too much and wasn't reusable/extensible. The new `dir.lua` core plugin is very simple, and thus we have a nice opportunity to ensure that it is reusable as a basic UI component for anything that wants to: 

1. present a "listing" of a directory-like concept
2. navigate-into the items of the listing
3. other stuff? (these actions decide the "extension points" we will need)

Use cases:

- browse a [github.com tree](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/tree/master/src)
- browse a local git tree
- remote ssh system
- zip archives

## Expected behavior

`dir.lua` can be reused by arbitrary plugins to present non-filesystem "dir listing" UIs.

## Related

- https://github.com/justinmk/vim-dirvish/issues/62
- https://github.com/justinmk/vim-dirvish/issues/249

comment_data.body:
I think this would be best informed by a particular ask, such as "allow dir.lua to be used to  browse zip archives."

is zip a good candidate to flesh this out in?
Yeah sorry, haven't had much time lately for open source work. I'll try to see if I can pick up that PR and integrate dir.lua. Or someone else can take ovef the work if they want.
vim.ui.tree is related but orthogonal, I think? The tree-view of dir.lua will use vim.ui.tree, but dir.lua itself is a higher-level component
What would plugins gain using dir.lua instead of directly using `vin.ui.tree`?

I am breaking this down as follows:

1. implement basic api for builtin plugin consumers (zip/archive.lua)
2. update such plugin consumers (i.e. ship #39246, which I will take over)
3. wait for stable apis
4. (maybe) ship public way to consume dir.lua + docs (is this within scope?)

> What would plugins gain using dir.lua instead of directly using `vin.ui.tree`?

all of the current `dir.lua` behavior, which doesn't use `vim.ui.tree` at all: mappings, buffer management, cursor positioning, events... and whatever other concepts find their way into the "dir browser" topic.

> What would plugins gain using dir.lua instead of directly using `vim.ui.tree`?

I think you are asking the wrong question.

IIUC vim.ui.tree would differ primarily from dir.lua (and I'm just speculating - since it doesn't even exist yet xd) in aesthetics alone.

dir.lua is also  _simpler_ than `vim.ui.tree`.

Accordingly, dir.lua is the natural precursor/entrypoint for any builtin plugin consumer before it could even move to vim.ui.tree, if it should at all.

This just sounds to me like `vim.ui.tree` would be the Lua interface to the functionality offers. Thus basically all functionality dir.lua currently offers dan eventually be lifted to `vim.ui.tree` (opening its interface) and dir.lua then becomes a thin "directory listing" layer on that. 

> Accordingly, dir.lua is the natural precursor/entrypoint for any builtin plugin consumer before it could even move to vim.ui.tree, if it should at all.

Basically this yes, but I don't think we should make dir.lua (a plugin which users can disable!) the entrypoint for other plugins.

you might be right, not sure. I had assumed that `vim.ui.tree` would be strictly for presenting a "tree" layout. but i suppose nothing is stopping us from "abusing" it for the non-tree mode of `dir.lua`, by only feeding it 1 "level".

it will become more clear once we know what "hooks" are needed. also keep in mind, `vim.ui.tree` doesn't address these parts of the `dir.lua` interface:

- mappings,
- buffer management,
- events

those are all higher-level concepts than what a tree "widget" would do.

> Basically this yes, but I don't think we should make dir.lua (a plugin which users can disable!) the entrypoint for other plugins.

Yeah I was thinking this too. For example, layering archive.lua on top of dir.lua creates that implicit requirement. It will take some thought. Like, should what it someone enabled archive.lua but disables dir.lua :thinking: I am not aware of this pattern in the existing codebase. But I do think it is elegant!

Anyways, #40482 is up for now...

> Like, should what it someone enabled archive.lua but disables dir.lua

disabling dir.lua shouldn't be supported. the only thing we need to support is allowing another plugin to "own" `filetype=directory`

> disabling dir.lua shouldn't be supported. the only thing we need to support is allowing another plugin to "own" filetype=directory

shall I remove `loaded_nvim_dir_plugin` then?

~~if we need to then yes. not urgent atm.~~

eh, i suppose we should do it now so people don't get confused. is there any defensible reason people need to disable it, i.e. does dir.lua "get in the way" somehow? as long as another dir browser can "own" dir-browsing, `dir.lua` shouldn't be a problem.

The default key mapping can be a problem? Because I had the below, neovim would complain at start up. Had to delete the key mapping along with `augroup`.

```lua
local remap = vim.keymap.set
local opts  = { noremap=true, silent=true, unique=true }
remap('n', '-', function()
  return require('mini.files').open(vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(0))
end, opts)
```

yeah we might be stuck with `g:loaded_xx` until we have a real mechanism for saying "don't enable plugin xx" https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/34704 . that is kind of hinted at in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40489 which councils an `after/...` approach, which is not great 🙈
